ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The case is a rider-initiated cancellation on a RydeX booking, so it enters only through NS-0's rider branch: cancelled_by = rider [F2], and the fee can only be tested under NS-4, not under the driver no-show provisions [F2][NS-0]. The trace settles that the rider cancelled 100 seconds after acceptance (12:54:00 → 12:55:40) [F2], which is inside the 3-minute free-cancellation window of NS-4, so no $6.61 cancellation fee could arise on this trip [F2][NS-4].

Independently, no arrival-based charge exists on this record: driver_arrived_at is null [F3], the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival [F4], and the closest approach to the pickup was 2138 m, never within 200 m [F1]. NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii) therefore both fail [F4][F1][NS-1], and where NS-1 fails the fee must be refunded in full under NS-2 [F2][NS-2]. The driver's written "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F8] is a statement, not a system record, and cannot cure the missing arrival record; the platform records [F3][F4] control.

The amount follows the trace formula: the cancellation fee on the fare record is $6.61 [F5], with surge 1.0× so nothing else attaches [F6]; 1 × $6.61 = $6.61 [F5][F6][NS-4]. That single fee is the contested item, so it is refunded in full [F5][NS-7].

No account flag attaches: NS-2's flag requires a driver who tapped "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius, and here no tap occurred at all [F2][F4][NS-2]. The rider's two prior upheld no-show disputes [F12] and the driver's clean record [F13] are profile facts and decide nothing [F12][F13][NS-0].

Safety screen: I read every message in the file — the complaint (driver "nowhere near", a lateness objection) and the driver's statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F8] — plus the absence of any chat [F7]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and no safety issue is in dispute [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. Evidence suffices: the timeline and fare records settle both the NS-4 timing and the NS-1 preconditions [F2][F4][F5].

rejected_claims.reason: No basis for an account flag: NS-2's flag requires the driver to have tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup radius, but the record shows no tap and no automatic arrival [F4] and a closest approach of 2138 m [F1], i.e. he never claimed arrival at all; NS-4/NS-3 place no breach on the driver here [F2][NS-2][NS-4].

Accurate as stated but adds nothing the ruling needs — the fee is disposed of on the NS-4 3-minute window alone [F2][F3][NS-4]; the driver's lateness [F1] is not used as a ground, so this claim neither supports nor blocks the refund.

The driver's clean profile [F13] does not decide the case and does not prevent the refund the system records require [F1][F3][F4][F5][NS-4]; profile facts cannot be used to retain a fee that no clause authorises [F13][NS-4].
